messages_2:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AtlasHealth redlines — security exhibit + audit requests (attached)

Thanks Monica — quick thoughts from product/legal ops perspective. I think a single consolidated reply that includes the following will keep this moving: 

- SOC 2: Offer SOC 2 Type II report for the most recent 12-month period under NDA. We cannot agree to continuous access to raw reports; propose view-only via a secure portal or provisioned PDF with redactions for third-party vendor details.

- Audit rights: Limit to one (1) third-party audit or inspection per 12 months, scoped to systems and services used to host AtlasHealth's data. Audits to be remote by default; any onsite visit requires 30 days' notice and approval (and cost allocation). We should require reasonable security and non-disclosure obligations for any auditor.

- Pen test reports: We should not provide full underlying vendor or partner reports. Proposed compromise: provide an executive summary, scope, and remediation confirmation. If customer insists on a full report, require a written request, mutual NDA addendum, and ability for us to redact demonstrably third-party-sensitive detail.

- Evidence cadence: Propose quarterly remote evidence packages (summary of changes, relevant logs/controls snapshots) and a SOC 2 report annually. For ad-hoc evidence requests, require a 10-business-day SLA and limit scope to items relevant to AtlasHealth's environment.

Suggested snippet for the security exhibit (high level):
"Vendor shall provide Customer with Vendor's most recent SOC 2 Type II report covering the services used by Customer; access will be provided under mutually agreeable confidentiality terms and limited to Customer and its designated third-party auditor. Customer's audit/inspection rights (if any) shall be limited to one (1) audit per twelve (12) month period, conducted during Vendor's normal business hours and scoped to systems and services that process Customer data. Any audit request requiring onsite access shall be subject to Vendor's prior approval and cost recovery for Vendor's reasonable expenses."

I'll draft a redline and send by EOD. If Legal prefers different thresholds (e.g., 45 days for remediation), flag it here.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Agree with Karthik's framing. From Legal: we should be explicit about the allowed auditor qualifications, confidentiality, and a remediation-first flow. I drafted language and attached a redline for the security exhibit. Key legal points: 

- Define "Permitted Auditor" as an independent third party with ISO 27001 or equivalent credentials and bound by a written confidentiality agreement.
- Audit scope: "systems and services used to provide the Services to Customer"; exclude multi-tenant underlying infrastructure beyond what processes Customer data.
- Timing & remediation: Auditor provides findings to Vendor; Vendor has 45 days to remediate material findings; Customer may escalate only if Vendor fails to remediate in good faith.
- Evidence delivery: Remote evidence bundle (logs, config snapshots) delivered within 10 business days of request, limited to data relevant to Customer.

Attachment: proposed_redline_security_exhibit.docx

I also added a short paragraph preserving our right to protect third-party-sensitive information and a clause requiring Customer to return or destroy any sensitive vendor reports after review.

If everyone is good, Monica — can you propose this externally as our formal position and offer a short call with Atlas Legal to walk through expectations? Laura, if you have additional comment, please add.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
General Counsel (acting), Redwood Inference
